title: Maximum Prime Difference
summary: Given an integer array, find and return the greatest distance between the indices of any two prime numbers within the array.
statement: Given an integer array, find and return the greatest distance between the indices of any two prime numbers within the array.
constraints: nums contains at least two positive integers and includes at least one prime value.
Distance is the absolute difference between array indices containing prime numbers.
Return the maximum such distance; with one prime position the result is zero.
hints: The farthest pair of qualifying indices is always the first and last prime occurrence.
Scan from each end using a square-root primality test.
Find leftmost prime and rightmost prime, then return right-left.
Every prime index lies between those extremes, so no other pair has greater index distance.
editorial: Every prime index lies between those extremes, so no other pair has greater index distance.

tests.explanation: The first prime is at index one and the last at index four, giving distance three.
Only eleven is prime, so both selected prime indices are three and the distance is zero.
